entries.name: Hobgoblin
entries.content:
Appearance

Hobgoblins are said to be taller than their goblin cousins, reaching to the height close to adult humans.
Abilities

Possessing the acute hearing and night vision as regular goblins, Hobgoblins are superior to the former in every way, such as in height and also in intelligence. Hobgoblins are also capable of articulating and carrying out complete sentences in a legitimate conversation.[1]
Known Hobgoblins

Agu
Trivia

Hobgoblins are comfortable in regards to living with their goblin brethren, even allowing adoption.
Jugem was mistaken by one of the Re-Estize Kingdom's soldiers for being a hobgoblin as he is considered to be bigger and stronger than a normal goblin.[2]
A hobgoblin also appears in the Web Novel, leader of the remnants of a goblin tribe that was destroyed by the Sunlight Scripture and Black Scripture.[3]

entries.name: Redcap
entries.content:
Redcaps (レッドキャップ) are a variant of goblins from YGGDRASIL that can be summoned through either using a Horn of the Goblin General under specific conditions or a special book found in Nazarick's library Ashurbanipal.


ADVERTISEMENT
Appearance

Redcaps are described as evil and twisted looking goblins. Barring weapon difference aside, every Redcap variant seems to commonly wear a pointed red hat and steel boots.
Abilities

Redcaps have the ability to hide within their summoner's shadow and possibly their target too for that matter. At the same time, they can even go as far as reemerging out of that person's shadow if ordered to and then carry out their surprise attack.[1]

A Redcap's primary weapon in battle seems to vary among its summoners. For starters, while the ones summoned by Enri wielded long scythes, the ones summoned by Lupusregina were equipped with axes instead.

According to the author Maruyama, they lack long-ranged attacks, and cannot win in long-distance fights. However, since the Redcaps usually fight together as a unit especially in Enri's Goblin Army with exceptionally high morale, it was impossible to exploit their weakness.[2]
Trivia

A Redcap in Scottish folklore is a malevolent, murderous goblin that is said to inhabit ruined castles especially where there were once the scenes of tyranny or wicked deeds and is known for soaking its cap in the blood of its victims.
Enri has thirteen of these beings as a division called Goblin Bodyguards serving under her leadership in the Goblin Army.
Lupusregina conjured thirty Redcaps that were estimated to be level 43. She also heavily hinted on the fact that these Redcaps are the lowest-leveled goblins summonable in Nazarick's library.
According to Maruyama, Enri's Redcaps are around the same level as Lupusregina’s Redcaps.
Redcap's ability seems to be exactly similar to that of the Shadow Demon's ability.
Maruyama notes that if a rogue/thief type character left their racial class levels as they are now, it will allow them to become a Redcap. Afterward, not also using the Red Cap classes ability, can result in the character participating in a class event that leads to the acquisition of a special class within the setting. Only one player in YGGDRASIL has ever attained that class after Redcap.[3]
In the Web Novel, Redcaps are referred as Red Hats (レッドハット

entries.name: Vah Un
entries.content:
Background

Similar to Puri Uns, Vah Uns are water-controlling beings. They were one of many races that Jaldabaoth enslaved as part of his demi-human coalition to attack the Roble Holy Kingdom.[1]
Appearance

Vah Uns are an ogre-like race. A Vah Un's skin color was said to be bluish-white. In addition to that, a Vah Un had a single thick horn on its forehead.[2][3]
Abilities

Vah Uns have water-linked special abilities such as transforming into a mist to avoid an enemy's ranged attacks from afar without receiving damage. However, there is a limit to the Vah Uns' ability as it can only defend against seven ranged attacks for a certain duration of time and no more than that amount.

Nevertheless, they were considered as the kind of beings which possessed very good overall fighting power and a shocking amount of stamina. One of the warriors from the Vah Un race was skilfully using a mace during its fight with both Neia Baraja and CZ2128 Delta.[4]
Active

Water Splash: A ball of water that is shot out at the intended target.
Fog Cloud: A bank of fog that covers up the surrounding.

entries.name: Bafolk
entries.content:
Appearance

Bafolk looks like bipedal goats, wearing chain shirts and typically carrying large spears.[1][2]
Background

Bafolk are a demi-human species that live in mountainous regions.

They were one of many races that Jaldabaoth enslaved as part of his demi-human coalition to attack the Roble Holy Kingdom. 
Abilities

Bafolk legs are every bit as capable as a mountain goat, making them fearsome warriors who could scale even city walls if they had so much as the slightest bump or depression on their surface. The spears Bafolk are equipped with, are long enough that they could stab people passing underneath prison camp watchtowers from above.

Bafolk fur tangled on slashing swords and steadily blunted their edges, so after killing one, it was important to clear the fur off the blade.
Culture

Bafolk have their own calendar system that differs from the human calendar based on horns. They tend to live in tribes and war with one another, at least that was the case until Buser came along and united all of the Bafolk Tribes under his leadership.

entries.name: Magelos
entries.content:
Magelos (マーギロス) are a demi-human race living in the Abelion Hills.


ADVERTISEMENT
Background

Magelos were one of many races that Jaldabaoth enslaved as part of his demi-human coalition to attack the Roble Holy Kingdom.
Appearance

The Magelos are similar to humans in appearance save that they possess four arms. In the Anime they are shown to have long spiny necks, four eyes and two toed clawed feet.[1][2]
Abilities

Magelos are born with the ability to use spells of up to the 4th Tier. The spells they could use apparently appeared on their bodies like tattoos. Their more powerful members were covered in tattoos. Sometimes, there were individuals who could develop skills as magic casters, and those were rumored to be able to cast spells of up to the 5th Tier. They might be Lord-level entities.[3]
Culture

Magelos did not eat humans, finding it disgusting, given that they were visually similar to humans

entries.name: Pteropus
entries.content:
Pteropuses (プテローポス) are a demi-human species native to the Abelion Hills.


ADVERTISEMENT
Background

Pteropuses are species which lived on cliff sides, who were very adept at long-distance gliding.

They were one of many races that Jaldabaoth enslaved as part of his demi-human coalition to attack the Roble Holy Kingdom.
Appearance

The Pteropus had bat-like membranes for hands and rose almost vertically. In the Anime they resemble bipedal pterodactyls.[1][2]
Abilities

While Pteropuses can fly, it seemed to require a lot of strength, so they could only fly for a while every day, and after that, they could not even glide. If Pteropuses did not fly, they could rend armor with the wind, so defending against it was very difficult. Pteropuses are a species which was strong when they could not fly.

entries.name: Stone Eater
entries.content:
Background

Stone Eaters were one of many races that Jaldabaoth enslaved as part of his demi-human coalition to attack the Roble Holy Kingdom.
Appearance

The Stone Eaters look similar to apes, with long white hair.[1][2] In Mass for the Dead, Stone Eaters are depicted as more monkey-like with patches of rock-like skin and long prehensile tails.
Abilities

Stone Eaters are armed with crude weapons. In a way, their most frightening feature is their ability to spit the rocks they ate. The stone fragments they could easily spit in excess of one hundred meters could put dents in metal armor with ease. However, they could only do so a limited number of times, so if one could endure through it, it is not a problem.[3]

Elite members can gain a special buff to physical abilities depending on mineral types they eat. For instance, by eating diamonds, they could temporarily gain physical damage resistance which could only be bypassed by bludgeoning attacks. Usually, only three such abilities could be active at once.[4]
Culture

Very little is known about the Stone Eaters' culture, save that they are tribal. In its hierarchy is a king that rules them above all others.
Known Stone Eater Tribes

Lagon
Known Stone Eaters

Halisha Ankara
Jajan
Trivia

Their ability to enhance themselves by consuming mineral is similar to the Quagoa

entries.name: Spidan
entries.content:
Background

Spidans were one of many races that Jaldabaoth enslaved as part of his demi-human coalition to attack the Roble Holy Kingdom.
Appearance

Spidans are arachnoid-like demi-humans with four long and slender arms and legs that resembled spiders.[1][2]
Abilities

Spidans could spit all sorts of silk from their mouths and make all manner of clothes and items with that silk. The silk clothing they made in this way was as hard as steel.[3][4]
Trivia

The Zerns used Spidan Webbing in advance to hold down the shelves used to tie the rope that both Neia and Delta used to infiltrate the castle the captured Zern prince was held

entries.name: Horuner
entries.content:
Background

Horuners were one of many races that Jaldabaoth enslaved as part of his demi-human coalition to attack the Roble Holy Kingdom.
Appearance

Horuners possess horse-like legs who were adept at sprinting. In the Anime they appear as satyr-like creatures with human as well as equine-like facial features.[1][2]
Abilities

Horuners could run for long periods without rest and possessed shocking mobility.[3]
Trivia

Based on their description Horuners seem similar to fauns or satyrs from Greek mythology.

entries.name: Chaos Beast
entries.content:
Background

Chaos Beasts are endemic to the New World, appearing after the Great Tomb of Nazarick transferred from YGGDRASIL during the Catastrophe. They appear from purple fissures that erupt spontaneously throughout the regions and even in Nazarick.[1] These monsters serve as some of the major antagonists in the ruined New World as the three surviving nations: Re-Estize Kingdom, Baharuth Empire, and Slane Theocracy struggle to rebuild.[2]
Types of Chaos Beasts

Quadruped Chaos Beast
Warrior Chaos Beast
Giant Chaos Beast
Double Sword Chaos Beast
Giant Flying Chaos Beast
Mochi Type Beast
Kadomatsu Type Beast
Dragon Chaos Beast
Spear Chaos Beast
Mimic
Appearance

These creatures resemble creatures made of amethyst colored metal and crystal, which appear as Chaos Stones. In other rare cases, these stones are embedded in the center of their bodies.
Abilities

Chaos Beast Logo
Chaos Beast Icon
Chaos Beasts are noted to be stronger than average monsters, and their appearances greatly vary from one another.[3] A few powerful types are mostly humanoid and wield weapons and other special abilities and seem to hold general sway over the lesser breeds. Chaos Beasts seemingly appear from the Cracks, which are also able to bypass the defenses of the Great Tomb of Nazarick, prompting the NPCs to be always on guard in case of an attack. In addition unlike other monsters, that fight on instinct or reason, Chaos Beasts will prioritize strong targets based on their level of power. On average most Chaos Beasts are above the difficulty rank of 50 based on the Adventurer's difficulty level for monsters.[4]

Based on Nazarick's experiments it's hypothesized that they possess some sort of sense to help them locate possible prey. Instant death spells can affect these creatures, though experiments have shown this to be the case for ordinary Chaos Beasts and not specialized ones.[5]

Recently it was observed in the archipelago where the Mysterious Island is located, and were a Crack was located deep underground, releasing large numbers of Chaos Beasts, that as per usual Chaos Beasts will dispersed to the surrounding area to hunt any organisms. However after eliminating their target prey in the immediate area, and lacking any new prey, Chaos Beasts may have a tendency to wait near the Crack that gave birth to them.[6]

Upon defeat, a Chaos Beast's body will dissipate, leaving only a Chaos Stone.[7] According to Momonga, these Chaos Stones are very similar to an item drop like a Data Crystal from YGGDRASIL.[8]

Strangely from representatives from a group called the Mercenary Knights, the threat of the Chaos Beasts are not just limited to the New World, but they have also appeared in another world. And although their presence in the other world is minimal compared to the New World, it is still heading slowly towards destruction.

Some Chaos Beasts like the Mimic are indirectly birthed from a phenomena which occurs when there is constant travel within the Womb Corridors, Cracks, which causes the anomaly to undergo defragmentation and cause the space to produce copies of beings taken into the Chaos Zone, though the spawning is said to take place in a special place in the dimension.[9]
Known Chaos Beasts

Shiramochi-ō
Frozen Giant

entries.name: Mimic
entries.content:
Appearance

Mimics are a unique type of Chaos Beast that are actually shapeshifters, taking the form of other beings.
Abilities

While mimics appear to possess possess flawless shapeshifting abilities, they appear to have limited intelligence, as they can only parrot words and not use speech. They are very fragile and thus rely on tricking their victims. So far it has yet to be determined if they mimics can replicate the abilities of those they impersonate.

Oddly enough unlike normal Chaos Beasts, which can be detected through Divine Right, these monsters do not give of any strange presence. Due to this Demiurge wonders if perhaps this is because Mimics are of the same nature as the components in the Crack.

According to Aggresiel and Billiophia, they believe the Mimic is possibly a byproduct of the "Calamity of Cracks" that occurred in E-Rantel, in where multiple Cracks or Womb Corridors opened up and sucked hundreds of people. According to them as more things pass through the Crack in a given period of time, the anomalies experience distortions, and experience a phenomena called defragmentation which leads to the copies of the victims who were taken into the Crack.

And while rescuing the victims of the Crack, bringing them out of the anomaly won't stop the birth of the Mimics, its suspected that the Mimics are spawned in a specific area of the Womb Corridor which needs to be eliminated to prevent the spread of these monsters.

The real origin of the Mimics are revealed to be the direct result of Remnant, a mineral which could grant wishes within the Chaos Zone or Womb Corridor. The root of it all being strong desires. Of the Mimics that appeared being Nigun Grid Luin, Leinas Rockbruise, and Brain Unglaus they are all what humans could call heroes of the Theocracy, the Empire, and the Kingdom. Those who wished for them were the people who were abducted into the Womb Corridor. In other words, the thoughts of the many "humans" trapped within the Crack, seeking salvation, may have led to the Mimics arising. A similar case would be Shiramochi-ō, who manifested through the wish of unknown creators and attacked Nazarick at a specific time.

Still, according to the Mercenary Knights the Mimics are the first case they've seen where Remnants reacted without even being touched. Thus leads to a question if activation of a Remnat's wishing power is a matter of numbers, or the level of urgency.

Additionally the abilities and actions of the Mimics who have the appearances of these many heroes were somewhat lacking. Which suggests that the wishes from Remnant could copy the was the general appearance of the heroes and grant them primitive speaking abilities. But it seems that if the thoughts of many people are at work, then perhaps the psychology of those who fear heroes, such as criminals, is also at work.[1]
Trivia

Mimics appear to be similar to doppelgängers, though unlike the latter don't seem to possess the form of telepathy that allows them to read the beings they impersonate.
Momonga compares Mimics to the copies or replicas conjured by Enhela Read Gahi.
It's suspected that something or someone may have created the Mimics using the abducted people who were taken into the Chaos Zone.
When killed, Mimics leave behind a Chaos Stone, which according to the protagonist, when using Divine Right appears to have a different color.
After these creatures were discovered in the Chaos Zone by the Sorcerer Kingdom, what information initial discovered was shared with the military forces of the Quadripartite Alliance, who realized the threat they creatures posed, Hence they began to develop code phrase for security purposes.[2]
There are future plans by the Sorcerer Kingdom to deploy golems to guard against Mimics in E-Rantel.[3] And due to their threat all veteran adventurers were standing guard in the city to guard against the monsters. And even the effectiveness of Nazarick's defense network controlled by the Defense Tree was checked to fight against this new threat

entries.name: Black Scripture
entries.content:
Black Scripture (漆黒聖典) is one of the Six Scriptures of the Slane Theocracy. They were said to be the strongest scripture among the Six Scriptures.


ADVERTISEMENT
Background

Black Scripture is the Slane Theocracy's final trump card, a special forces unit comprising of individuals with heroic-level abilities. One could even think of them as a group supposedly made up of adamantite-ranked adventurers. However, there was actually a critical difference that sets the Black Scripture apart from most adamantite adventurer groups, that of their equipment used by each of its respective members. In other words, they're utilizing the equipment that originated from the arsenal of items belonging to the Six Great Gods. While so, the Black Scripture are commonly assigned to very dangerous tasks, and so they had a very high attrition rate.

Their title as the mightiest unit within the Slane Theocracy and their black motif directly correlate with them following the teachings of the God of Death of the Six Great Gods, Surshana. Not only is their Death God the most powerful of all the Six Great Gods, but their group as a whole also holds the greatest fighting power than all the other Five Scriptures too.
Chronology

The Undead King Arc

Main article: The Undead King Arc
While the Sunlight Scripture was attempting to assassinate Gazef Stronoff, the Black Scripture was preparing for the upcoming resurrection of Catastrophe Dragon Lord, while protecting the artifact known as Downfall of Castle and Country.[1]

The Bloody Valkyrie Arc

Main article: The Bloody Valkyrie Arc
The Black Scripture were dispatched to the area near E-Rantel after the divination spell on Nigun Grid Luin was countered. Taking it to be an indication of the Dragon Lord, they came to investigate. The Black Scripture proceeded to run into a pack of vampire wolves. Soon after they encountered Shalltear Bloodfallen. Sensing the danger, Kaire used Downfall of Castle and Country to brainwash the vampire. However, she was mortally wounded while two of her bodyguards were killed before Shalltear completely lost her mind.[2]

The Lizard Man Heroes Arc

Main article: The Lizard Man Heroes Arc
After being forced to retreat from their encounter with Shalltear, the Black Scripture returned back to the homeland. There the Captain of the Black Scripture gave his report to the Six Cardinals of the strange vampire his comrades had encountered near E-Rantel.[3]

The Invaders of the Large Tomb Arc

Main article: The Invaders of the Large Tomb Arc
Platinum Dragon Lord warned Rigrit not to have her ring fall into the hands of the enemy, particularly the Black Scripture.[4]

The Ruler of Conspiracy Arc

Main article: The Ruler of Conspiracy Arc
The Black Scripture has been reportedly badly weakened after its clash with Shalltear by the Supreme Council of the Slane Theocracy.

Additionally, one of the Six Cardinals suggested sending the Black Scripture's retired members over to the Dragon Kingdom as reinforcements. In other words, they were hoping to have the retirees assist that nation against the face of a demi-human invasion.[5]

The Craftsman of Dwarf Arc

Main article: The Craftsman of Dwarf Arc
The Elf King reminisced about the past, where he once captured the Theocracy's trump card and impregnated her and how she was later saved by the Black Scripture. He thinks about going to the Slane Theocracy to retake the child he sired.[6]

The Witch of the Falling Kingdom Arc

Main article: The Witch of the Falling Kingdom Arc
After the Kingdom went to war with the Sorcerer Kingdom, which the former would surely lose, the Theocracy deployed several members of the Black Scripture, led by Quaiesse Hazeia Quintia, to the doomed country. However, rather than coming to the nation's aid, they were instead ordered to recruit powerful adventurers to the Theocracy's cause in exchange for escorting them out of the Kingdom safely.

One of the adventurer groups they approached was Blue Roses, alongside Red Drop's Azuth Aindra. Unfortunately, talks between the Black Scripture and Azuth instantly broke down when the latter keep bombarding the secret organization with confidential questions they are not open to neither talk about nor answer it. Similarly, all the members of Blue Roses have also turned down the Black Scripture's offer, instead choosing to stay behind and defend the Kingdom. In the end, although the Back Scripture failed to recruit the Kingdom's two adamantite-ranked adventurer groups, many other adventurers accepted their offer as planned.

After Azuth made a mocking statement about Rufus and his connections to them and the Theocracy, the Black Scripture quickly turned hostile to all the adamantite adventurers present in the room. It was said that the members of the Black Scripture did not lower their guard since then as they left the meeting room. They maintained that kind of attitude in a way if the group of adventurers were to take any sort of action on them, they would retaliate in kind.

With the meeting over and done with, the Black Scripture made it their plan to report and relay what Azuth of Red Drop said to them to the higher-ups when they returned back to their nation.[7]

Principles

While part of the greater whole of the Slane Theocracy, the Black Scripture has its own separate culture that reflects the edicts of their patron god respectively. According to the laws dictated by the Six Great Gods, someone over the age of twenty will already be considered an adult in the Theocracy. Thus, when junior Black Scripture members go out on missions, they would wear magical masks to conjure a fake face.

Additionally, when the time came for a new Shaman Princess to replace their old one, the job of the Black Scripture was to remove the Crown of Wisdom from its current wearer. Thereafter, they would then promptly send off the now-insane Shaman Princess to be with the Six Great Gods. In other words, the Black Scripture was tasked with the job of killing the previous user of that item once they served their purpose.[8]

During important missions, the Black Scripture was also apparently given the authority to use the powerful "Divine Equipment" left behind by the Six Great Gods of the Theocracy for vital assignments. Additionally the Scripture members are given the added duty of protecting the item’s user during their missions until its power can be activated. As seen where they were assigned to protect Kaire during their mission to subjugate the Catastrophe Dragon Lord until she activated the item’s power in order to bring the Dragon Lord under their control.

Due to her being its strongest member of the Black Scripture, its Extra Seat, "Zesshi Zetsumei" was stated to to be granted access to the personal armory of the Six Great Gods. With it being implied that she was specifically trained in a special job classes in order to allow her use of their equipment and allow her to use the skills of the Six Great Gods via her Talent when combined with the items. As shown during the last stages of the Theocracy - Elf War, Zesshi was granted usage of the equipment of the "God of Wind" and the "God of Death" respectively in her successful attempt at the Elf King's life.
Strength

Black Scripture is considered to be the strongest group among the Six Scriptures and consists of members who have reached human physical limits and possess heroic level strength. In other words, Black Scripture is the strongest of all combat groups working within the Slane Theocracy and its pride. Unlike the other Scriptures, each of its members focuses on a specific type of combat or skill and is comparable to a whole combat group. They will usually carry out their missions alone, but will still work together if ordered by their captain.

According to Nigun Grid Luin, only the Black Scripture could eliminate many Archangel Flames like Ainz Ooal Gown which is a demonstration of their group's strength. However, unlike Ainz, he had doubts that any of those members from the Black Scripture would be able to take care of all the angels with just one spell. [9]

The highest-ranking and strongest members of the Black Scripture are thought to be demigods, because of their immense powers and the fact that the blood of the Six Gods runs within them. Upon meeting them, Shalltear Bloodfallen estimated the strength of their group's leader to be superior to Solution Epsilon, a member of the Pleiades. The cardinals stated that the Black Scripture can use a grand ritual to summon the highest-ranked angel in case their group's strength isn't enough to eliminate a threat.

During the meeting of four members of the Black Scripture with Blue Roses and Azuth Aindra, it was immediately noticed by the Adamantite Adventurers that each and every one of the four members' individual strength alone far surpassed theirs by a wide margin despite their own immense power. Thereby showing that a single member of the Black Scripture has power equivalent to a team of Adamantite Adventurers.

To be inducted into the Black Scripture, candidates needed to reach the "Realm of Heroes" which was over level 30. Those in other Six Scriptures who managed to reach such an achievement would then be transferred into the Black Scripture.
Known Members

Current Members

1st Seat: Captain of the Black Scripture
2nd Seat: Time Turbulence
3rd Seat: Four Great Spirits
4th Seat: Divine Chant
5th Seat: Quaiesse Hazeia Quintia, "One Man Army"
6th Seat: 6th Seat of the Black Scripture
7th Seat: Thousand Leagues Astrologer
8th Seat: Cedran, "Myriad Barriers"
9th Seat: Beaumarchais, "Divine Chain"
10th Seat: Strongest Human
11th Seat: Infinite Magic
12th Seat: Heaven and Earth
Former Members

Former 9th Seat: Clementine, "Windstride" (Defected)
Former 3rd Seat: Raymond Zarg Lauransan (Retired)
Former Extra Seat: Antilene Heran Fouche, "Certain Death" (Captured)

entries.content:

Spoiler Alert
Spoiler Alert: WARNING! This page happens to contain a lot of heavy spoilers that are all originated from the Overlord Light Novel series written by the author Kugane Maruyama. To every Anime-only watchers and Manga-only reader out there viewing this warning, please mindfully consider your decision first before choosing to expose yourself on reading the information below. If you're not currently up-to-date with the main source material in the official books, do consider staying away from the page for non-spoiler sake until you actually read it first ahead of time.




Slane Theocracy (スレイン法国) is a human nation of the New World and one of the three nations that neighbors Nazarick. One of the strongest countries in the region; it is a highly religious and orthodox state that promotes human supremacy, prompting them to often interfere in other nations' affairs for the "greater good of humanity".

ADVERTISEMENT
Background

Overlord II EP01 090
The Theocracy's geographical location
Being one of the oldest established human nations, the Slane Theocracy has a history of six hundred years based on fierce adherence to their country's religion. The doctrine of the Slane Theocracy revolves around the Six Great Gods, who appeared six hundred years ago. As a result, the country is divided into six different religious sects, each with its own specialized intelligence agency focusing on one expertise they're skillfully good at. Each sect is devoted to one of the Six Great Gods by the Scripture group's color.

Despite being split into different factions, the groups will still co-operate when necessary during times of crisis. They all acknowledge the threat of demons and other races in the world. Additionally, the Slane Theocracy's civilization is said to be more advanced in technology than any of the neighboring countries that surround it. The Slane Theocracy also has an institutionalized divine magic training system that is comparable with the Baharuth Empire in terms of arcane magic, one in which they possess a magic school that focuses on training faith-based magic casters. The overall literacy rate for citizens living in the Theocracy is fairly high.[1]
Humanocentrism

Overlord III EP06 104
The Theocracy's discrimination against non-humans
Although the Theocracy promotes the discrimination of non-humans and the supremacy of humanity, it only serves to be a tactic from the higher-ups in order to unify all humans with a common goal and increase their national power. Unlike the common folk, the high officials aren't blinded by xenophobic beliefs and prioritize the survival of humanity. In order to protect humans from the threat of other races, they have decided to bind people together with faith in the Six Great Gods. It is to this point where they have tried to keep all God-Kin within their country's borders, even going as far as to detain their wives/potential mothers.

At the same time, the Cardinals recognize the fact that their nation's philosophy has a flaw to it. They fear that their nation's ideology might lead them in a dangerous direction if the Theocracy ever ends up being bordered next to a powerful non-human nation like the Argland Council State. The Cardinals believe that it can play a major factor in radicalizing the citizens to come together and form a militant movement against that nation. Since this event is the worst-case scenario, the common folk will possibly shout for war with the Council State in order to destroy the enemies of mankind.

The citizens of the Slane Theocracy often view people with nonhuman ancestry living in their country as second-class citizens.[2]

Theocracy - Elf War

Despite the Theocracy's prejudice towards non-humans, the nation once had a friendly relationship with the neighboring Elf Country. However, this relationship came to an end over a century ago when the Elf King abducted and impregnated the ace of the Theocracy's Black Scripture. Fortunately, the Theocracy rescued her and the child that was forced upon her grew up to become the Theocracy's strongest God-kin.

Afterwards, at the urging of the child, a war of retribution was waged against the Elves. However, despite their superior military strength, the Theocracy's progress is slow since the Elf Country is mostly hard-to-traverse woodland and they do not want to waste their full forces on the war effort, resulting in the war still going on by the time the Re-Estize Kingdom fell. Elves have also become favored products in the Theocracy's slave trade.

Conspiracies

In order to achieve their goal of allowing humanity to survive in the face of demi-human threats, the Theocracy has been secretly manipulating the affairs of other human nations for what they believe is the greater good.

One of their actions was to shepherd the Re-Estize Kingdom, a human nation completely protected from demi-human nations by its neighbors and natural barriers. They believed this would allow the Kingdom to safely raise powerful individuals. However, their peaceful lifestyle instead caused many nobles to grow corrupt, resulting in the Kingdom becoming a failed state.

Deeming the Kingdom to be a failure, the Theocracy shifted its focus to the Baharuth Empire. Since the Theocracy couldn't directly take control of the Kingdom lest they share a border with the Argland Council State, which would inevitably lead to a war, they instead planned on letting the Empire conquer them.

Chronology

The Undead King Arc

Main article: The Undead King Arc
Overlord EP04 052
The Theocracy's failed assassination attempt on Gazef
The Slane Theocracy decided to take action to further their agenda over the Re-Estize Kingdom by assassinating Gazef Stronoff, the kingdom's strongest warrior and the main obstacle for Re-Estize's conquest by the Baharuth Empire. To accomplish this task, the Sunlight Scripture was dispatched to lure Stronoff while aided by the foolish nobles of the Nobility Faction, who were easily manipulated to think that this was their own plan.[3] During the operation, the Theocracy had the Sunlight Scripture under observation. However, for some reason, they lost the whereabouts of the entire force.[4]

In addition, the Theocracy had received a prophecy of the Catastrophe Dragon Lord's resurrection. In response, the Black Scripture was deployed to slay it. The Theocracy even lent them their nation's secret weapon, the World Item of the Six Great Gods; the Downfall of Castle and Country.

The Dark Warrior Arc

Main article: The Dark Warrior Arc
Overlord EP05 117
Clementine steals the Crown of Wisdom and goes rogue
A disaster struck the Theocracy when one of the Black Scripture members, Clementine, stole one of the Six Gods' treasures, the Crown of Wisdom, and went rogue. In response, the Windflower Scripture was sent out in pursuit of her to retrieve the item and execute the traitor.[5]

The Bloody Valkyrie Arc

Main article: The Bloody Valkyrie Arc
Overlord EP10 114
The Black Scripture is defeated by a powerful vampire
Another disaster struck the Theocracy when the Black Scripture encountered a powerful vampire. While the Black Scripture managed to partially brainwash the creature, this only caused it to indiscriminately attack anyone who approached it, forcing the Scripture to retreat.[6]

The Lizard Man Heroes Arc

Main article: The Lizard Man Heroes Arc
After the Black Scripture retreated back to the Theocracy, the captain had a meeting with the Cardinals. In the end, to avoid unnecessary losses, it was decided to let the vampire be and have a standard observation team monitor it before gathering their forces and confronting it again. The Cardinals also figured that, if someone capable of defeating that monster were to appear, they would have to strengthen their national defense.[7]

The Magic Caster of Destroy Arc

Main article: The Magic Caster of Destroy Arc
Overlord III EP10 004
The Theocracy declares neutrality in the Kingdom and Empire's Annual War
The Theocracy learned that the Baharuth Empire had formed an alliance with the newly-founded Sorcerer Kingdom, led by Ainz Ooal Gown, for their Annual War with the Kingdom. Not wanting to make an enemy out of him, the Theocracy sent a message to the Kingdom acknowledging his claim to E-Rantel and declaring neutrality in the conflict.[8]

Later, when a human boy threw a stone at Ainz while the latter was claiming E-Rantel, Momon believed he might have been [Charmed] and his action was part of a Theocracy plot to incite revolt.[9]

The Ruler of Conspiracy Arc

Main article: The Ruler of Conspiracy Arc
Overlord IV EP03 042
The Supreme Council meets
During a Supreme Council meeting, after learning of the Massacre at Katze Plains, it was decided that staying neutral in the Annual War was the right choice. Weighing their options, the Council decided that the Theocracy would continue to focus on their war with the Elf Country while sending spies to the Sorcerer Kingdom. They also wanted to bring former Black Scripture members out of retirement and dispatch them to the Dragon Kingdom as an aid.[10]

Later, Emperor Jircniv arranged a secret meeting with emissaries from the Theocracy in hopes of forming an alliance against the Sorcerer Kingdom. However, when Ainz Ooal Gown arrived unannounced, the emissaries assumed the Emperor had betrayed them and angrily left. Afterward, the Theocracy cut all ties with the Empire.[11]

The Craftsman of Dwarf Arc

Main article: The Craftsman of Dwarf Arc
To speed up their invasion of the Elf Country, the Theocracy deployed the Holocaust Scripture to the battlefield. With them on the front lines, the nation is expected to overtake the elves in a few years.[12]

The Witch of the Falling Kingdom Arc

Main article: The Witch of the Falling Kingdom Arc
Overlord IV EP10 051
The Black Scripture is sent to the falling Kingdom to rescue Adventurers
The Theocracy had sent several spies to infiltrate the Sorcerer Kingdom. Unbeknownst to them, however, the nation's leadership was fully aware of their presence, but chose to merely observe their movements for now.[13]

When the Sorcerer Kingdom went to war with the Re-Estize Kingdom, the Theocracy sent the Black Scripture to the latter country when its defeat was certain. However, rather than aid them, they were instead ordered to recruit adventurers by offering them sanctuary. In the end, while they failed to get some key individuals, many accepted the offer and migrated to the Theocracy.[14]

The Half Elf God-kin Arc

Main article: The Half Elf God-kin I
and The Half Elf God-kin II Arc

Following the Kingdom's downfall, the Cardinals met for an emergency meeting. With the increasing encroachment on human territories by non-human countries, it was decided that the Theocracy must play an even more active role in the defense of humanity than it already was. However, they were once again confronted by logistical issues. On top of having lost contact with the spies they had sent to the Sorcerer Kingdom, the Theocracy's military was currently occupied with their ongoing war with the Elf Country. Therefore, to end the conflict as swiftly as possible, the Cardinals approved a plan to assassinate the Elf King.[15][16]

Volume16Illustration003
The Theocracy assassinates the Elf King
The invasion of the Elf Country was not only to avenge the honor of the Theocracy, but also out of a long-term plan to use the territory of the elves as a shelter for the Theocracy's civilian populace in the inevitable war with the Sorcerer Kingdom. Having already researched the elf trees used by the elves, the Theocracy intended to conquer the capital to use it to evacuate their people. However, the largest elf tree settlement was near Crescent Lake and they needed the city intact so the higher ups forbade their armies from devastating the area. The Theocracy eventually launched a full-out assault on the elven capital, overwhelming the defending elves despite the latter receiving reinforcements from their dark elven brethren.[17]

In the end, the Theocracy's plot was mostly successful, with the Elf King being killed and the Elf Country conquered. However, the Sorcerer Kingdom interfered in the war, which resulted in their assassin being captured. They consequently learned of the Theocracy's involvement in the incident with the brainwashed vampire, who is one of the Sorcerer King's direct subordinates, prompting them to begin preparing for war.[18]

Culture

The Theocracy has a population of 15 million. The nation preaches human supremacy and the persecution of other "lesser" races. With its religion revolving around the Six Gods and their descendants, the Theocracy is effectively divided into six different religious sects, each with its own unique culture and practices. One factor all six groups share is that the names of the people in the Slane Theocracy consist of a given name, a baptized name, and a family name.

In Mass for the Dead, it was revealed that the Theocracy follows a seniority system. Unlike other nations out there, they do not possess a culture that aims for reward. Instead, the people of the Slane Theocracy live to express their faith.[19]

The current ideology espoused by the members of the Slane Theocracy, that only humans should flourish, and every other race is an enemy, even if they were humanoids, is not the original policy. This policy is comparatively new and has only been practiced for a century plus a few decades. Before that, the Theocracy also took the other humanoid races into consideration, upholding a policy that they should join hands together and fight against the other races. However, for various reasons, the vision of the nation was altered to this current xenophobic attitude.
Religion

In addition to worshiping the Six Great Gods, the citizens of the Slane Theocracy hold their descendants in veneration. The preservation of their gods' bloodline is of the utmost priority and they make an effort to ensure their legacy carries on to the next generation. To achieve this, the Theocracy practices polygamy. Not only is such a practice considered to be a rare occurrence, but the husband is also restricted to have two wives at most.

Another central part of the Slane Theocracy's religion is the Miko Princesses, who, by description, are the nation's religious figures vital in performing some of their important rituals. So far, there seem to be Six Miko Princesses, which are related to the elements of the Six Great Gods. Though seemingly an esteemed position of power, in contrast, it appears that the Miko Princesses are effectively living sacrifices. They are chosen from the population with great care and scrutiny, due to the items they are given from their pedestals, which pose many risks to the user.

In the Web Novel, the Six Miko Princesses comprise of the Miko Princess of Water, the Miko Princess of Fire, the Miko Princess of Wind, the Miko Princess of Earth, the Miko Princess of Light, and the Miko Princess of Darkness. Likewise, all of them are users of priest-type 5th tier magic, but this is a national secret.[20]

There also exists a special temple dedicated to the God of Water. Within this temple is a special chamber filled with water called "Eye of the Water God."[21]
Politics

Overlord EP13 110
The Six Cardinals of the Six Great Gods
As a Theocracy, the Slane Theocary is governed by a Pontifex Maximus with a position similar to that of an Emperor, elected in a conclave by the Six Cardinals.

The Pontifex Maximus is assisted by a board of advisers from the highest executive authorities in the Slane Theocracy, the Supreme Executive Council. It consists of the representatives of the Six Great Gods, the Cardinals, and from the government the heads of Executive, Legislature, and the Judiciary, plus the head of the Research Institute in charge of magic affairs, and the Grand Marshal as the highest appointment-holder in the military. The council sits at a round table within a sacred room where everyone is equal. There are no superiors or inferiors on the table, everyone is a collaborator and a comrade, including the Pontifex Maximus.

Overlord IV EP03 019
Six Cardinals in Conference
Cardinals are the highest appointment holders of the six sects that are devoted to the Six Gods. The position of a Cardinal is higher than that of a representative of governmental affairs; the demerit is that they get no wages so that people aspiring to become Cardinals would not be motivated to rise through the ranks by greed. Hence, there were many individuals who took high office with the intention of serving their nation. The current Cardinals are:

Berenice Nagua Santini, the Cardinal of Fire.
Zinedine Delan Guelfi, the Cardinal of Water.
Dominic Ihre Partouche, the Cardinal of Wind.
Raymond Zarg Lauransan, the Cardinal of Earth and commander of the Six Scriptures.
Yvon Jasna Delacroix, the Cardinal of Light.
Maximilian Oreio Lagier, the Cardinal of Darkness.
There were only two countries that had the capability to set up national-level organizations. One of the two was said to have been the Slane Theocracy.
Military Strength

The knights from the Slane Theocracy are said to be far stronger than those of the Baharuth Empire.

Additionally, there are God-kin among them with great influence over the country. These special individuals are viewed as demigods who are descendants of their ancestors known as "players." When compared to both the Kingdom's or Empire's clerics, the Theocracy's faith-based magic casters (clerics) are usually more skilled than any of them. The average skill levels in the Theocracy are generally quite high. Also, the Theocracy has at least five artifacts left behind by the Six Great Gods.

In the Web Novel, if compared with purely human countries, the Theocracy possesses the strongest national power of them all due to its powerful military presence. Let alone their national power, the Theocracy also has the top fighting ability on the continent than any other human country. For instance, they conduct military operations within the nations bordering the Theocracy with the intention of suppressing demi-humans and other races. On the other hand, the Theocracy is capable of conducting large-scale rituals or have the highest class of priest to cast resurrection magic.[22]

The Slane Theocracy is also shown to have access to the Six Miko Princesses, whose usage of the Crown of Wisdom allows them to perform High-Tiered Magic normally impossible for humans to use or achieve.

entries.name: Argland Council State
entries.content:
Argland Council State (アーグランド評議国) is a demi-human nation located northwest of the Re-Estize Kingdom and surrounded by mountains. It is regarded as one of the two superpowers of the region, alongside the Slane Theocracy.


ADVERTISEMENT
Background

The Argland Council State, usually referred to as simply the "Council State", is located northwest of the former Re-Estize Kingdom. It was founded by the Platinum Dragon Lord, Tsaindorcus Vaision, as part of his experiments with communities, being one of the nations formed following the defeat of the Evil Deities two hundred years ago. It is a mixed-race nation inhabited by various human and demi-human species all living together harmoniously.

As the name implies, the nation is led by a council composed of representatives of each race inhabiting the country. There are also five Dragon Lords that are a part of the council, known as the "Five Dragon Councilors", who are said to be very powerful and help guide the nation by passing their wisdom down to its citizens.
Web Novel

In the Web Novel, the demi-humans that are part of this country are comprised of various races. For instance, Panasolei Gruze Day Rettenmaier stated that there were goblins and ogres who reside in their nation.[1] Also it appears that marine races like the Sea Lizardmen and Mermen are also members of the Council State.[2]

Chronology

The Dark Warrior Arc

Main article: The Dark Warrior Arc
The Argland Council State was briefly mentioned by the Swords of Darkness as they listed the various prominent figures in the New World.[3]

The Lizard Man Heroes Arc

Main article: The Lizard Man Heroes Arc
While reviewing a map of the New World with Albedo, Ainz concluded that Nazarick would have to be careful with approaching the Argland Council State, likely wary of the Dragon Councilors that rule it.[4]

The Invaders of the Large Tomb Arc

Main article: The Invaders of the Large Tomb Arc
After Nazarick took control over Eight Fingers, Ainz noted that the tomb still had very little information available regarding the Council State.[5]

When the various Worker groups hired to raid Nazarick discussed the strongest individuals they know of one of them brought up the Dragon Lords leading the Council State. Also, when comparing the strength of human warriors, the Workers decided to exclude the Council State's swordsmen, since they are mostly composed of demi-humans.[6]

After Aura and Mare invaded the imperial palace of the Baharuth Empire with their dragons, someone almost mistakenly thought it was one of the Council State's Dragon Councilors.[7]

The Ruler of Conspiracy Arc

Main article: The Ruler of Conspiracy Arc
When Ainz tried to convince Pluton Ainzach of humans need to coexist alongside other races, he makes a comparison to the Council State with its diversity of races living peacefully together.[8]

Later, during a conference of the Slane Theocracy's leadership, it was noted that the reason why they had not conquered the Re-Estize Kingdom themselves was that would leave them bordering the Council State, which would inevitably lead to war.[9]

The Witch of the Falling Kingdom Arc

Main article: The Witch of the Falling Kingdom Arc
The Council State was said to be actively negotiating with the Re-Estize Kingdom for an alliance against the Sorcerer Kingdom.[10] Unfortunately, during the emergency meeting held after the Sorcerer Kingdom declared war on the Kingdom, when King Ramposa III asked how talks with the Council State were progressing, Crown Prince Zanac regretfully informed his father that nothing had been agreed on yet, effectively leaving the Kingdom to fend for itself.

After news of the Sorcerer Kingdom's declaration of war became public, the Council State was one of the nations that the Kingdom's citizens who could afford it considered fleeing to, due to its proximity. However, the Karsanas City-State Alliance was ultimately the more popular option, as it had a higher human population.[11]

Unbeknownst to the Kingdom, while the Sorcerer Kingdom claimed that they would commence with their invasion in a month, they had already begun their attack, focussing mainly on the nation's northern regions to cut them off from the Council State.[12]

While their attempt at an alliance had fallen through, one of the Council State's Dragon Councilors, Tsaindorcus Vaision, still ended up coming to the Kingdom's aid by attempting to assassinate the Sorcerer King, although he was likely acting on his own here. Unfortunately, the attempt failed and, despite operating under an alias, Demiurge managed to deduce his connection to the Council State.[13]

The Half Elf God-kin Arc

Main article: The Half Elf God-kin I
and The Half Elf God-kin II Arc

The Slane Theocracy's Cardinals believed that the Council State would not interfere with their plot to assassinate Elf King Decem due to the nation's poor relationship with the Elf Country.[14]

Culture

The nation appears to be composed of demi-humans, humans being a minority. In fact, humans made up less than 10% of the country’s population.
Religion

It is currently unknown what the Council State's primary religion is. However, since it is a nation composed of various races, it likely has similarly numerous amount of religions.
Politics

The Council State is the only known democracy in the New World. It functions on a loose parliamentary system, with each race inhabiting the country typically holding a single seat and the person who gets to represent their kind being chosen through a periodic popular vote amongst said race. However, Dragon race is exempt from this "one seat per race rule", with them instead having five representatives, known as the "Five Dragon Councelors", who each hold a permanent seat in the parliament.

The Council-State is also one of only two nations in the region capable of setting national-level organizations.
Military Strength

As of yet, there is no concrete knowledge or evidence of the Argland Council State's military background. However, it was noted that this nation is one of the few places where Wild Magic may still be practiced. From the perspective of the Slane Theocracy's Cardinals, they were said to be very powerful, with the Platinum Dragon Lord being among their councilors.

In the Web Novel, the country seems to enlist Dragon Knights in their ranks. As well as the adventurers are mostly comprised of demi-humans.[15] There are about four adventurer parties that are around the same rank as Blue Roses.[16]
Foreign Relations

Despite the Council State being one of two military superpowers of its region of the New World, the other being the Slane Theocracy, it has historically only had minimal interaction with the neighboring human nations, perhaps fearing potential retaliation from their counterpart. After the founding of the Sorcerer Kingdom, however, the Council State has begun to take a more active role on the international stage.
Slane Theocracy

According to the Theocracy's leadership, citizens of the Council State and Theocracy actively hate each other. This is mostly due to the Theocracy's doctrine promoting discrimination against demi-humans, prompting the Council State to hate them right back in kind.

However, both nations are aware of their military limitations and thus hesitant to wage open war against each other, which would most likely result in mutual destruction. In a way, the two nations keep each other in check, with neither being willing to overreach out of fear of provoking the other. The Council State particularly tries to restrict the movements of the Theocracy's God-kin.

Overall, despite their extremely tense relationship, the Council State and Theocracy still maintain political dialogue with each other.

Baharuth Empire

According to Jircniv Rune Farlord El-Nix, the Baharuth Empire maintains political dialogue with the Council through its ministry of foreign affairs.

Sorcerer Kingdom

After the founding of the Sorcerer Kingdom, the Council State seems to regard them as a severe threat to the New World. As a result, one Dragon Councilor, Tsaindorcus Vaision, had been actively pushing for a military alliance with the Kingdom against the Sorcerer Kingdom. However, the other Dragon Councilors and regular Councilors had been more hesitant to take an aggressive stance, seemingly preferring to remain neutral while maintaining a political dialogue with the nascent country. Unfortunately, as a result of Tsaindorcus' attempting to assassinate the Sorcerer King without his fellow councilors' consent, tensions between the Council State and the Sorcerer Kingdom are likely to only escalate further.

Re-Estize Kingdom

The Kingdom was the Council State's neighbor to the south and served as a buffer country between itself and the Theocracy. Perhaps because of this, the Council State had seemingly little-to-no political dialogue with the Kingdom for the longest time, fearing potential retaliation from the Theocracy.

However, following the founding of the Sorcerer Kingdom, the Council State attempted to form an alliance with the Kingdom against their mutual foe. Unfortunately, talks were progressing slowly, with not many councilors being sold on the idea, causing the Alliance to ultimately not be formed on time before the Sorcerer Kingdom began their conquest of the Kingdom. Afterward, the idea of an alliance was seemingly abandoned, since it was the Kingdom who technically instigated their conflict with the Sorcerer Kingdom.

Despite their attempt at a military alliance falling through, at least one councilor still came to the Kingdom's aid by attempting to assassinate the Sorcerer King. However, it seems that the said counselor acted on his own and the rest of the Council State's leadership had no intention of aiding the Kingdom.

Elf Country

While the Council State's exact relationship with the Elf Country is unknown, the fact the Slane Theocracy's Cardinals believed that they would not interfere with their attempt to assassinate the Elf King implies that the two nations are not on good terms.

Known Characters

Five Dragon Councillors

Spoiler Alert: WARNING! This page happens to contain a lot of heavy spoilers that are all originated from the Overlord Light Novel series written by the author Kugane Maruyama. To every Anime-only watchers and Manga-only reader out there viewing this warning, please mindfully consider your decision first before choosing to expose yourself on reading the information below. If you're not currently up-to-date with the main source material in the official books, do consider staying away from the page for non-spoiler sake until you actually read it first ahead of time.



Dragon Kingdom (竜王国) is a human nation of the New World. It was founded by the Brightness Dragon Lord and is currently ruled by his great-granddaughter, Dragon Queen Draudillon. They have have been facing invasion from the neighboring Beastman Country in recent years, prompting them to turn to other nations for military support.

ADVERTISEMENT
Background

The Dragon Kingdom was founded by the Brightness Dragon Lord. Taking a human as a mate, the Dragon Lord created the royal family line of their nation. By doing so, the dragon granted all its descendants access to the long-forgotten power of Wild Magic.
Beastman Invasion

Despite the Kingdom's rich heritage and history, it faces constant harassment from the neighboring Beastman Country, whom raids the Kingdom to use humans as a food source. In recent years, the raids have turned into an all-out invasion, with the Beastmen intending to conquer the Dragon Kingdom followed by other human nations. Currently, the Beastmen have already taken several cities, forcing the Dragon Kingdom to request for military aid from the Slane Theocracy and the Baharuth Empire.

Chronology

The Lizard Man Heroes Arc

Main article: The Lizard Man Heroes Arc
Among the countries and cities listed in the New World's incomplete map obtained by Ainz Ooal Gown, the Dragon Kingdom happens to be one of them alongside Sea City. He noted that a powerful Dragon had formed the Dragon Kingdom in the past, and apparently its royalty has inherited that person’s bloodline.[1]

The Magic Caster of Destroy Arc

Main article: The Magic Caster of Destroy Arc
The current ruler, Draudillon Oriculus talks with her advisor about the dire state that the Dragon Kingdom currently finds itself in. Draudillon wonders about their lack of aid, in particular why the Slane Theocracy has yet to send its Sunlight Scripture like it usually does. Her advisor then informs her that a certain magic caster founded a nation and declared war on the Re-Estize Kingdom, but she just dismissed it claiming they should focus on the troubles of their own nation.[2]

The Witch of the Falling Kingdom Arc

Main article: The Witch of the Falling Kingdom Arc
When the Sorcerer Kingdom declared war on the Re-Estize Kingdom the seal of several other nations could be found on the official document, including the Dragon Kingdom. The Kingdom's foreign affairs department investigated the document and concluded that it was the genuine seal of the Dragon Kingdom.[3]

The Half Elf God-kin Arc

Main article: The Half Elf God-kin Arc
It has been established that the Dragon Kingdom has opened official diplomatic relations with the Sorcerer Kingdom and have even purchased undead from said nation in order to combat their current war with the beastmen nation.

The Slane Theocracy council have also thought about sending the rescued adventurers from the Re-Estize Kingdom to the Dragon Kingdom in order to help them with their war efforts. After calling into a vote, it was decided they will be allowed to do so and if any of them wished were freely allowed to stay there.[4]

Culture 

It seems that the Dragon Kingdom is in a dire financial crisis, due to heavy reliance on foreign military aid to protect their country's borders and the increased expenditure on their military in fending off the invading beastmen.
Religion

Currently, nothing is known regarding the Dragon Kingdom's primary religion. However, the fact that is was founded by Brightness Dragon Lord might imply that they worship Dragon Lords.
Politics

The Dragon Kingdom appears to be an absolute monarchy, with most if not all political power being in the hands of the monarch. In this case, said monarch is a direct descendant of the country's founder, Brightness Dragon Lord, known as the "Dragon King" or "Dragon Queen". The monarch is also accompanied by a personal adviser who seems to serve as the representative of the common people. However, said advisers hold no political power of their own, with ultimate decision-making remaining solely in the hands of the monarch.
Military Strength

Because of constant attacks from the Beastman Country and having to rely on the Slane Theocracy and Baharuth Empire for military aid to fend them off, it can be assumed that Dragon Kingdom's own military strength is in very bad shape. It likely does not have the funds to build up a good military, because they have to pay ransom to the other nations in return for their aid. Starting by the fact that there is a big difference in the basic strength of humans and beastmen, next to the continuous attacks and the big military spend, all those factors make it difficult for the government to increase the power of their armies.
Foreign Relations 

The Dragon Kingdom is heavily dependent on other countries for its defense and protection as the country is unable to fund a decent military of its own. Fortunately, all the other human nations recognized that the Dragon Kingdom is the only obstacle that keeps the advancing beastmen at bay. In addition, the Queen personally enlists the local adventurers to support defending the kingdom.
Slane Theocracy

The Dragon Kingdom pays tribute to the Slane Theocracy each year in order for the Theocracy to dispatch troops against the Beastman Country. With financial backing, they would usually lend military aid to the Dragon Kingdom when dealing with the demi-human invasion. However since the Sunlight Scripture who normally would be dispatched to support the Dragon Kingdom was dissolved, the nation was left without aid. SInce then the Dragon Kingdom has turned to the Sorcerer Kingdom for support.

The higher ups of the Theocracy did not believe that the Dragon Kingdom opening diplomatic channels with the Sorcerer Kingdom to be favorable. To avoid being marginalized, the Theocracy assigned additional support to prevent the Dragon Kingdom from totally relying on the enemy nation. To further help them in there war effort, they decided to provide military aid by sending the rescued adventurers to the Dragon Kingdom to provide aid.

Baharuth Empire

The Baharuth Empire is a neighboring state of the Dragon Kingdom, though relations between the two powers seem sour due to its emperor having a personal dislike towards the Kingdom's monarch. Though it does send military aid, albeit with reluctance, not out of charity but as a necessity. In fact, the Dragon Kingdom's existence is what's keeping the Beastman Country from invading the Empire's territory.

Sorcerer Kingdom

When Dragon Queen Draudillon was first informed about the founding of the Sorcerer Kingdom, she initially just ignored it. However, at some point, the two nations seem to have formed a proper diplomatic relationship.

After a noble from the Re-Estize Kingdom attacked one of the Sorcerer Kingdom's transports, the Dragon Kingdom approved of their declaration of a war of retribution. The Kingdom's ministers believed that the reason for this was because the Dragon Kingdom sought to curry favor with the Sorcerer Kingdom.

They have started opening diplomatic ties with the nation and have even started to purchase powerful undead from which means that formal economic trading has also started between the two nations. As noted by the Slane Theocracy, the Dragon Kingdom itself is likely using these powerful undead to defend their homeland from the Beastman Country. Worrying the Theocracy as it will cause the Dragon Kingdom to become more and more reliant on the Sorcerer Kingdom.

Re-Estize Kingdom

Although their exact relationship was unknown, the Dragon Kingdom approved of the Sorcerer Kingdom's declaration of war against the Re-Estize Kingdom after the latter's nobles attacked one of their humanitarian aid transports. Although not specified, the Kingdom's ministers hypothesized that the reason why they turned their back on them, despite being a fellow human nation, was because the Sorcerer Kingdom offered more appeal and they no longer saw any benefit in continuing relations with the relatively weak Kingdom.

Beastman Country

Currently the Beastman Country and the Dragon Kingdom is currently in open hostile warfare. It was the kind of situation where the beastmen native to the Beastman Country are attacking, conquering, sacking and abducting the Dragon Kingdom's territory, cities, villages and towns in order to obtain the human populace of the Kingdom. This invasion was initiated by the beastmen who seek to capture humans as a stable food source.

Currently the Dragon Kingdom is having immense difficulty fending off the Beastmen due to the superior racial advantages the Beastmen possess in comparison to their human armies. Because of that situation not in their favor, it forced the Dragon Kingdom to rely on foreign aid from other human nations to fend them off along with Adamantite Adventurers.

So far, the Beastmen Country have successfully conquered three cities of the Dragon Kingdom and are holding numerous flesh banquets where they gorge on their abundant acquired human flesh. In a way, their overall advancement was said to have put the Dragon Kingdom in a dire state.
