Spoiler Alert: WARNING! This page happens to contain a lot of heavy spoilers that are all originated from the Overlord Light Novel series written by the author Kugane Maruyama. To every Anime-only watchers and Manga-only reader out there viewing this warning, please mindfully consider your decision first before choosing to expose yourself on reading the information below. If you're not currently up-to-date with the main source material in the official books, do consider staying away from the page for non-spoiler sake until you actually read it first ahead of time.




Dwarf Kingdom (ドワーフの王国) is a nation of dwarves residing in earthen halls within the Azerlisia Mountains. The country has long been in conflict with the Mountains' native Quagoa tribes until the dwarves struck a trade deal with the Sorcerer Kingdom and they routed the demi-humans out.

ADVERTISEMENT
Background

The history of the Dwarf Kingdom starts more than two hundred years ago. The country remains almost completely isolated from the world for a long time until the era of the Thirteen Heroes emerges. At that time, the dwarves cities prospered and that was deemed to be the golden era of the Runecraft.

However, those years ended when the nation was attacked by one of the Demon Gods, who destroyed their ancient capital and forced its citizens to flee to survive. During the attack, most of the royal family members were killed, and the one who remained decided to leave the Kingdom to join the fight against the Demon Gods. Its last king was known as the Magic Craftsman and the Runesmith King, a hero immortalized in the legends.

Two hundred years ago, their nation consisted of four underground cities for which they had built and were spread all around the underground caverns of the mountains, each connected by a series of cave networks. However, prior to the current events, those cities have dwindled down to two.

The inhabitants of the Dwarf Kingdom are always in conflict with the Azerlisia Mountains' other inhabitants, particularly the mole-like demi-humans known as Quagoa.
Chronology

The Lizard Man Heroes Arc

Main article: The Lizard Man Heroes Arc
The Dwarf Kingdom is mentioned as one of many examples of information that Ainz as Momon had obtained from the Guildmaster of the Magician's Guild in E-Rantel.[1]

Zenberu Gugu mentioned to Zaryusu Shasha about a lesson he learned from the dwarves: friends who drink together become firm friends. He also learned a lot from a dwarf in his travels and how he received his signature war spear as a memento of their meeting.[2]

Zaryusu remembered some information about the Dwarves from Zenberu who stated that they were a mountain-dwelling species with exceptional skill concerning metal and the heroic legend of Magic Craftsman who founded the Dwarf Kingdom.[3]

The Invaders of the Large Tomb Arc

Main article: The Invaders of the Large Tomb Arc
When human nations discriminate on races such as the elves, dwarves were considered to be a special exception for the Baharuth Empire. Due to the trading relationship the Baharuth Empire had with the Dwarves, they were assured of fair protection under that nation's law. It was mentioned that in the Azellisia Mountains, the Dwarf Kingdom stood between the Re-Estize Kingdom and the Baharuth Empire.[4]

The Ruler of Conspiracy Arc

Main article: The Ruler of Conspiracy Arc
During Ainz's visit to the residence of the Martial Lord's promoter, Ainz sees the dwarven craftsmanship in Osk's collection. Its owner commented to him that the collection's piece that caught his attention was created by a dwarf craftsman of the Dwarven Kingdom about 150 years ago.[5]

When Demiurge's returns to Nazarick, he was informed by Albedo that Ainz had traveled to the Dwarf Kingdom alongside Shalltear and Aura as bodyguards.[6]

The Craftsman of Dwarf Arc

Main article: The Craftsman of Dwarf Arc
The Dwarf Kingdom found itself in peril when it was attacked by an unprecedentedly large army of Quagoa. After the Fortress at the Great Rift fell, leaving only the gate of Feo Jera to hold them back, it seemed that the Quagoa's victory was certain.[7]

However, the Sorcerer Kingdom just happened to have sent an envoy led by the Sorcerer King himself to the Dwarf Kingdom to discuss international relations. Upon request from the Commander-in-Chief of the Dwarven Army, the envoys lend their military strength and were successful in repelling the Quagoa.[8]

Afterward, the Regency Council met with the Sorcerer King to talk about setting up a trade relationship. The Sorcerer King offered to lend the Dwarf Kingdom his undead to use as a labor and military force in return for a part of the profits they would produce. He also offered to reconquer the ancient capital of Feo Berkana from the Quagoa and the Frost Dragons in return for the Dwarf Kingdom handing over all practitioners of Runecraft to the Sorcerer Kingdom. The Regency Council was hesitant to accept the Sorcerer King's offers, believing he wanted to use the Dwarf Kingdom and would destroy it if he saw no more use for it. However, they ultimately accepted, seeing that they needed to end the threat of the Quagoa.[9]

The Sorcerer King was successful in reconquering Feo Berkana, giving the Dwarf Kingdom its ancient capital back. The Regency Council honored their part of the deal and handed over all the runesmiths to the Sorcerer Kingdom. However, the Forgemaster of the Regency Council had stolen a piece of metal ingot of unknown value from the Sorcerer King and disappeared. This ended the first interaction between the two nations on somewhat of a bittersweet note.[10]

Shalltear's Travel Diary Arc

Main article: Shalltear's Travel Diary Arc
The Dwarf Kingdom is mentioned during the time when Ainz and his entourage rested in the fortress he conjured while heading towards the nation.[11]

The Paladin of the Holy Kingdom Arc

Main article: The Paladin of the Holy Kingdom Arc
Several dwarves were sent as technical advisers to help the Sorcerer Kingdom's skeletons pave roads in E-Rantel. According to dwarves living in the Sorcerer Kingdom, they stated the Dwarf Kingdom has begun using the undead for other purposes like manual labor other than military support alone.[12]

The Witch of the Falling Kingdom Arc

Main article: The Witch of the Falling Kingdom Arc
In Zanac Valleon Igana Ryle Vaiself's intel report, it was mentioned E-Rantel and the dwarven nation have initiated trade relations. Trading undead miners and fresh ingredients for ores and high-quality, dwarven-made farming equipment. Cargo hauling within the Azerlisia mountain range was handled by the undead, causing the shipping and labor costs to be basically negligible, so much so that it’s cheaper for them to buy from the dwarves than from the Re-Estize Kingdom.[13]

After the carriage attack had taken place, the Dwarf Kingdom was one of the five nations that had signed and agreed with the Sorcerer Kingdoms declaration of war with Re-Estize Kingdom. But the top brass had some trouble to verify its seal, as the one they had on record was an outdated version. They finally got clarification from their sources in Re-Blumrushur.[14]

The Half Elf God-Kin Arc

Main article: The Half Elf Gid-kin Arc
By the time of Ainz Ooal Gown’s visit to the Elf Country, the Dwarf Kingdom was said to be under the economic sphere of the Sorcerer Kingdom.[15]

Culture

The dwarves prefer to live in the underground caverns of the mountains and practice their craftsmanship.[16] Nonetheless, they don't seem to mind interacting with both human and demi-humans as they have formed trade relationships with the people of the Baharuth Empire and have interacted with the lizardmen of the Great Lake.

All dwarves love alcohol and most would spend a large portion of their wages to purchase it and even carry small flasks with them to work to take regular sips even if it is prohibited and is usually tolerated regardless.

The Dwarf Kingdom was the home of runecraft, which the runesmiths of old took pride in. However, the art had declined after the kingdom opened its borders to the outside world two hundred years ago. With the introduction of new magical techniques, primarily the much more efficient Tier Magic, runecraft became outdated and nearly forgotten.

The dwarves of the kingdom also enjoy bathing, unlike humans which is normally reserve for nobility. There are public bathhouses in each city, running off the heat from the crucibles of their forges, and the dwarves frequent them. It seems that not only the injured and sick but also miners after work go there during their off-time.[17]
Religion

It's unknown what sort of faith that the Dwarf Kingdom follows, however, there is a High Priest of Earth, who governs everything that has to do with magic. It is possible this position is related to the Temple of the Four Great Gods.
Politics

In the past, their nation was a monarchy ruled by the Runesmith King. However, the monarchy no longer exists after the last members of the royal bloodline left to fight against the Demon Gods and is now instead ruled by a group of eight dwarves called the Regency Council. However, the Regency Council seems to remain detached from the current state of affairs of the Kingdom and was unconcerned with the amassing Quagoa right outside their doorstep.

The current members of the Regency Council are:

The High Priest of Earth: Head of the Dwarven Earth Temple.
The Forgemaster: Head of the Blacksmith Workshop.
The Commander-in-Chief: Head of the Dwarven Military.
The Director of Food Production: Head of the Food Production.
The Cabinet Secretary: Secretary of the Regency Council.
The Brewmaster: Head of the Brewery Production.
The Master of Caves and Mines: Head of the Ore Mining.
The Merchant's Guildmaster: Head of the Foreign Affairs and Leader of the Merchant Guild.
Also, all mines within the Kingdom are nationalized meaning that any mineral excavated from these mines, by law that person has to make a payment to the government in order to keep it. However, it does not apply to any minerals excavated in abandoned mines and tunnels.
Military Strength

All military matters are handled by the Dwarven Army. The primary defense line for the dwarven capital is the fortress that lies just in front of a large gorge that separates the south from the north. The only primary access route to the dwarven capital is through the suspension bridge. Because of that, the fortress was built in front of the capital as enemies would be forced to concentrate their attacks there.

After establishing trade deals with the Sorcerer Kingdom, it was presumed that undead like the Death Knights, for instance, were implemented in the Dwarf Kingdom's defensive force. During the Regency Council meeting, one of the dwarves believed that their nation will have to continue relying on the Sorcerer King’s strength for the next few decades.
Foreign Relations

The Dwarf Kingdom is barely registered on the map. However, the Kingdom's runesmiths are infamously hailed as skilled craftsmen. Aside from establishing a few trading relations with their neighboring countries, the Kingdom seems to be very isolated that very few outsiders even know where the exact location of their country is positioned. This is not due to any form of bad reputations or self-imposed isolation. It is just that the dwarves are content with how things are and are not usually interested in matters that do not concern or involve their country.
Re-Estize Kingdom

The Kingdom had not attempted to forge any national-level ties with the dwarves for at least 200 years as any official documentation they have on is inscribed with outdated paperwork. However, the Kingdom's people do acknowledge their remarkable craftsmanship in creating items. Interactions with the Dwarf Kingdom was limited to small deals within the mining city of Re-Blumrushur.

When the Sorcerer Kingdom declared war with Re-Estize for attacking their grain supply carriages, the Dwarf Kingdom signed an official letter with their national stamp that showed they sided with the Sorcerer Kingdom and the Re-Estize was in the wrong.

Baharuth Empire

While slavery of non-humans is a common practice within the Baharuth Empire, all dwarves who find themselves in the Baharuth Empire are exempted from this rule due to the trade relationship between the Dwarf Kingdom and the Empire. However, even among the elites, very few people know the exact location of the country or anything about their culture. Interaction with them is usually restricted to occasional trade deals. About two hundred years ago, the dwarves exported their rune-craft weapons to the Empire and even its king visited, but a hundred years later all trade of rune crafted items ceased.

The current Empire now only engages in limited trade with the dwarves due to the lack of profit in doing so.

Sorcerer Kingdom

At first, the Dwarf Kingdom has had no interaction with the Sorcerer Kingdom. However, when Ainz got a good look at the dwarven craftsmanship, he was intrigued by the items that they created and has decided to visit the nation.

Ainz's visit coincided with the Quagoa invasion of the Dwarf Kingdom. Seeing a means to profit from the situation immensely, Ainz offered military aid from his country. During the negotiations, it was agreed that the Sorcerer Kingdom would provide the dwarves with undead labor, trade consumables, and military assistance to retake their ancestral capital in return for the dwarven runesmiths and ores.

After Feo Berkana was retaken, the majority of the dwarven people were impressed and had nothing but goodwill, and interest in visiting the Sorcerer Kingdom, when it was heard that both kingdoms would allow its citizens to travel freely between the two.

When the Sorcerer Kingdom went to war with the Re-Estize Kingdom, they fully supported the nation‘s justification and even sent an official letter with their own stamp to legitimize their own support.

United Quagoa Clans

The Dwarf Kingdom was in conflict with the Quagoa Clans due to mineral disputes found inside the Azerlisia Mountains. Their current relationship is so bad that it's basically kill on sight if one party as much as spots the other. After Ainz subjugates the survivors of the Quagoa Genocide, they are all taken to Nazarick. This has effectively ended the hostilities between the Dwarf Kingdom and the Quagoa.

entries.name: Supreme Beings
entries.content:
In Overlord, the Supreme Beings refer to the 41 original guild members of Ainz Ooal Gown, the powerful guild that ruled the Great Tomb of Nazarick in the game Yggdrasil. Here’s a breakdown of what they are and who they include:

🧙‍♂️ Who Are the Supreme Beings?
“Supreme Beings” is the term used by the NPCs (non-player characters) of Nazarick to refer to their creators, the players who designed and programmed them back when Nazarick was just a guild base in the game Yggdrasil.
In the world of Overlord, the NPCs view these 41 players as gods or divine creators and revere them with almost religious devotion.
After the game shuts down and Momonga is transported to the New World, he becomes the only Supreme Being remaining, under the new name Ainz Ooal Gown.
💀 Notable Supreme Beings
Out of the 41, only a few are named or described in the series:

Name	Role or Trait	Notable For
Momonga / Ainz Ooal Gown	Guild leader	The only one who stayed logged in until the shutdown; becomes the protagonist.
Touch Me	Strongest warrior	Wielder of the World Champion class, powerful Paladin. Inspired Momonga.
Ulbert Alain Odle	Black magic user	Designed Demiurge; loved destructive spells and chaos.
Peroroncino	Archer	Created Shalltear Bloodfallen. A pervert, but loyal guild member.
Bukubukuchagama	Slime VA	Created Aura and Mare. She was Peroroncino’s sister in real life.
Tabula Smaragdina	Alchemist	Created Albedo. Forgot to remove her “loves Momonga” trait.
Shizu Delta’s Creator	Not named	Created one of the Pleiades Battle Maids. Several others are unnamed.
🏰 Legacy in the New World
Nazarick's NPCs are extremely loyal to the Supreme Beings, and often compare the people of the New World to them, usually unfavorably.
Many of the floor guardians idealize the Supreme Beings, especially Ainz.
Some, like Albedo and Demiurge, are obsessed with fulfilling Ainz’s will, interpreting his vague commands as divine orders.

NPCs of the Great Tomb of Nazarick & Their Creators

👑 Guild Master

Ainz Ooal Gown (formerly Momonga)	Self-created (Momonga created his own character/avatar)
🛡️ Floor Guardians

Cocytus	5th Floor	Warrior Takemikazuchi
Demiurge	7th Floor	Ulbert Alain Odle
Aura Bella Fiora	6th Floor	Bukubukuchagama
Mare Bello Fiore	6th Floor	Bukubukuchagama

🧠 Area Guardians / Key NPCs
NPC	Role	Creator
Victim	8th Floor Guardian	Anonymous member (unknown)
Gargantua	4th Floor Guardian	System-created (not player-made)
Pandora’s Actor	Treasury Guardian	Ainz Ooal Gown (Momonga)
👩‍👧‍👧 Pleiades Battle Maids
NPC	Role	Creator
Narberal Gamma	Pleiades	Nishikienrai
Lupusregina Beta	Pleiades	Anonymous (likely)
Solution Epsilon	Pleiades	Herohero
CZ2128 Delta (Shizu)	Pleiades	Anonymous
Entoma Vasilissa Zeta	Pleiades	Kyouhukou’s creator (unknown)

🦴 Others in Nazarick
NPC	Role	Creator
Sebas Tian	Head Butler	Touch Me

🐉 Notes:
Several minor NPCs and monsters are also present in Nazarick, but many were created as generic units or by unnamed guild members.
There were 41 guild members in Ainz Ooal Gown, but only around half are named in the series.

entries.name: Maids
entries.content:
Pleiades (Battle Maids)

Elite combat unit made up of 7 powerful battle maids.
Personally selected by the Supreme Beings to protect Nazarick's 9th Floor and serve Ainz directly.
Strong NPCs with diverse combat abilities, each themed around a different personality or role.
🔸 Members:
Name	Notes
Narberal Gamma	Lightning magic user, adventurer alias “Nabe.”
Yuri Alpha	Calm and intellectual, uses martial arts.
Solution Epsilon	Sadistic slime, infiltrator specialist.
CZ2128 Delta (Shizu)	Silent gun-wielding automaton.
Entoma Vasilissa Zeta	Bug-themed maid with insect-based skills.
Lupusregina Beta	Energetic healer with a twisted side.
Aura Bella Fiora	Not actually a Pleiades, but sometimes associated because of the maid theme (usually not counted in official lineups). The true 7th Pleiades is Sebas Tian's non-canon assistant from a drama CD, but usually only 6 are shown in the anime/manga.
🧼 2. Normal Maids

Non-combatant homunculus-style maids.
Serve around Nazarick doing regular cleaning, cooking, laundry, etc.
There are 41 of them, one for each Supreme Being (although many of the creators left).
They lack combat skills and have basic personalities.
Still loyal to Ainz and Nazarick.
🧬 3. Homunculus Maids

Technically overlap with the "normal maids" category, but with more specific lore.
🔹 What makes them different?
They are mass-produced artificial beings, made via magical alchemy.
Very obedient, polite, and emotionless.
Created for manual tasks, not thinking or combat.
Usually seen in uniform lines bowing or tending to Nazarick’s guests or halls.
Used in various functions across Nazarick, especially on the 9th and 10th Floors.

entries.content:
Floor	Type/Theme	Guardian(s)	Notable Features
1st–3rd	Entry & Defense	No fixed Floor Guardian	Basic traps, low-level monsters
4th Floor	Underground Jungle	Gargantua (Special Guardian)	Huge golem, rarely used
5th Floor	Frozen Glacier	Cocytus	Ice palace, undead & frost monsters
6th Floor	Great Forest	Aura Bella Fiora & Mare Bello Fiore	Vast wilderness, wildlife, amphitheater
7th Floor	Volcanic Cavern	Demiurge	Hell-like area, experiments, demon army
8th Floor	Trap/Defense Floor	None (Various defenses)	Extremely dangerous traps and puzzles
9th Floor	Royal Quarters	Albedo (as Overseer)	Ainz’s residence, Pleiades battle maids
10th Floor	Throne Room	Ainz Ooal Gown	Throne of Kings, Guardian Council Room
💠 Detailed Floor-by-Floor Breakdown

🧱 1st to 3rd Floors – Entry and Defense Levels
Filled with low-tier traps, undead, and monster guards.
No main guardian.
Entrance to Nazarick and a place to test invaders.
🌿 4th Floor – Underground Jungle
A massive jungle terrain under a dome.
Guardian: Gargantua, a giant golem (not considered a true Floor Guardian, but a "strategic weapon").
Rarely moves unless ordered by Ainz.
Extremely powerful but emotionless and silent.
❄️ 5th Floor – Frozen Glacier
Covered in snow and ice, with an icy palace as its centerpiece.
Guardian: Cocytus, insectoid warrior and commander of Nazarick's armies.
Commands a legion of powerful warrior-type monsters.
Honorable and loyal, sees combat as sacred.
🌲 6th Floor – Great Forest
A vast forest area with various biomes and the coliseum.
Guardians: Twin dark elf siblings:
Aura Bella Fiora – Beast tamer, ranged combat expert.
Mare Bello Fiore – Druid-type magic user, shy and passive.
Hosts friendly beast-type monsters and amphitheater for events.
🔥 7th Floor – Volcanic Cavern
Fiery, infernal terrain filled with lava, demons, and laboratories.
Guardian: Demiurge, strategic genius and torture master.
Handles external operations for Nazarick and leads demonic subordinates.
In charge of the “Happy Farm” (a euphemism for horrifying experiments on humans).
☠️ 8th Floor – Death Trap Zone
No Floor Guardian, but possibly the most dangerous floor.
Filled with:
Deadly instant-kill traps
Puzzle-like obstacles
Rare monsters like Victim
Victim: A high-level angel who dies to activate massive area buffs/debuffs; used in emergency scenarios.
👑 9th Floor – Royal Quarters
Luxurious residential area for Ainz and his top NPCs.
Overseen by Albedo, the Overseer of Floor Guardians (not a floor guardian herself).
Home to the Pleiades Battle Maids.
Contains private rooms, lounges, and command facilities.
⚔️ 10th Floor – Throne Room
Contains the Throne of Kings where Ainz rules Nazarick.
Highest level of Nazarick; central to all command decisions.
Hosts the Guardian Meeting Room.
Only Ainz resides here permanently.
Highly defensible, with emergency backup systems.
⭐ Special Areas (Not Main Floors)

Arena (6th Floor Amphitheater): Used for duels or public demonstrations. The appearance of Amphitheater is a dreamy night sky of the Milky Way and the stars and nebulas

Treasure Vault: Guarded by Pandora's Actor, a shapeshifter created by Ainz himself.

Happy Farm (Demiurge’s lab): Hidden lab outside the usual floor layout.
Surface Graveyard: Above Nazarick; guarded by undead and traps.

Floor Guardian Chain of Command:
Albedo – Overseer of All Floor Guardians.
Floor Guardians (5th–7th, sometimes 4th & 6th).
Area Guardians & Subordinates – Under each Floor Guardian.

entries.name: Nazarick
entries.content:
What Is Nazarick?

The Great Tomb of Nazarick is the central base of operations for Ainz Ooal Gown and the strongest known dungeon/fortress in the Overlord universe.

Originally, it was a guild base in the DMMORPG Yggdrasil, created by the guild Ainz Ooal Gown, made up of 41 Supreme Beings (only Momonga/Ainz remained active at the end).
When Yggdrasil shut down, Nazarick and its NPCs were transported to a new fantasy world — E-Rantel and the New World.
In this world, Nazarick becomes a real place, and its inhabitants become sentient and fiercely loyal to Ainz.
🛡️ What Do They Protect?

The entire structure of Nazarick is designed to defend, protect, and serve the will of Ainz Ooal Gown.

🔹 1. Ainz Ooal Gown Himself
The main purpose of Nazarick’s defense is to protect Ainz, their ruler and the last remaining Supreme Being.
Every NPC and structure in Nazarick is loyal to him above all.
🔹 2. The Throne Room (10th Floor)
The most heavily protected area.
Symbolizes the heart of Nazarick and Ainz’s authority.
Home to the Throne of Kings and the meeting room of the Guardians.
🔹 3. Nazarick’s Secrets and Resources
Includes:
Magical research and artifacts
Wealth and rare items in the Treasury
Biological and magical experiments (like Demiurge’s "Happy Farm")
The dungeon's strategic weapons, like Gargantua and Victim
Protecting these resources is key to maintaining Nazarick’s dominance.
🔹 4. The Reputation of Ainz Ooal Gown
The Guardians are fanatically devoted to spreading Ainz’s glory and crushing anyone who disrespects or underestimates him.
Nazarick acts not just defensively but offensively to expand Ainz’s influence.
🧬 Who Protects It?

Role	Purpose
Floor Guardians	Control and defend each major floor.
Area Guardians	Manage smaller areas within each floor.
Pleiades Maids	Combat maids stationed on 9th Floor, protect residential areas and Ainz.
Albedo	Overseer of all Guardians; main protector of Ainz personally.
Pandora’s Actor	Protects the Treasury, can mimic other NPCs’ powers.
Victim	Sacrificial being who activates Nazarick’s ultimate defenses.
Cocytus & Demiurge	Lead external armies to deal with threats before they reach Nazarick.
💀 Why Is It So Important?
Nazarick is more than just a base. It is:

A holy place to its inhabitants.
A symbol of lost glory from the days of the Supreme Beings.
The center of power for the Sorcerer Kingdom (once Ainz declares himself King).
A near-impenetrable fortress, filled with traps, high-level monsters, and magic defenses designed to kill even the strongest invaders.
